'''Sonia M. Altizer''' (born 1970){{cn|date=May 2026}} is an American [[ecologist]] and professor at the [[University of Georgia]] Department of Entomology.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |title=Sonia Altizer |url=https://https/ |access-date=December 7, 2024 |website=University of Georgia |date=March 2018 |archive-date=June 25, 2020 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20200625000000/https://https//udn.com/news/story/121424/4659358 |url-status=dead }}</ref>

Her research includes work on animal migration, infectious disease dynamics, parasite transmission, urbanization, climate change, and butterflies.<ref name=":0" /> Altizer is a fellow of the [[Ecological Society of America]] and the [[American Association for the Advancement of Science]].<ref name=":0" /> At the University of Georgia, she is a Distinguished Research Professor and Department Head of Entomology.<ref name=":0" />

==Early life and education==
Altizer was born as the daughter of Jim and Chris Altizer of [[Watkinsville, Georgia]].<ref name=ocone>{{cite news|title=Sonia Altizer named UGA Athletic Association Professor in Ecology|url=http://www.oconeeenterprise.com/news/article_abb49ae0-4efe-11e4-b97e-c375eeb85f2b.html|accessdate=March 1, 2015|agency=The Ocone Enterprise|publisher=The Ocone Enterprise|date=October 8, 2014|archive-date=October 2, 2023|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20231002222116/http://www.oconeeenterprise.com/news/article_abb49ae0-4efe-11e4-b97e-c375eeb85f2b.html|url-status=live}}</ref> She grew up in York, Pennsylvania. Her passion for [[biology]] and the natural world began when she received a gift of a [[microscope]] and a grow-your-own-butterflies kit on her twelfth birthday.<ref name=tedxuga>{{cite web|url=http://tedxuga.com/sonia-altizer/|access-date=February 28, 2015|title=Ted x UGA|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150228001609/http://tedxuga.com/sonia-altizer/|archive-date=February 28, 2015}}</ref>

Altizer received a B.S. from [[Duke University]] in 1992 and a [[Ph.D.]] from the [[University of Minnesota]] in 1998. She also did a postdoctoral work at [[Princeton University]] and [[Cornell University]].<ref name="uga">{{cite web |title=Odum School of Ecology |url=http://www.ecology.uga.edu/facultyMember.php?Altizer-1/ |accessdate=February 28, 2015}}</ref>

==Career and research==
[[File:2012-07-20 15-16-40-Danaus plexippus.jpg|thumb|A [[monarch butterfly]], the subject of some of Altizer's research]]
For 20 years since a graduate student of the University of Minnesota, Altizer traveled the world to study [[monarch butterfly]] migration, ecology, and interactions with a [[protozoan]] [[parasite]]. She has researched how [[seasonal]] [[Lepidoptera migration|migration]] of these butterflies affects parasite transmission, and also developed collaborative databases of mammalian infectious diseases, on host behavior, ecology, and life history interact with global-scale patterns of [[parasitism]]. She also focused her research on songbird-pathogen dynamics, including studies of house finch [[conjunctivitis]], [[West Nile virus]], and [[salmonellosis]]. Altizer has published several publications and she recently co-edited a book that would be published in 2015, titled Monarchs in a Changing World: Biology and Conservation of an Iconic Insect. She also and participated in high-level task forces dedicated to monarch butterfly conservation. A citizen science project called Monarch Health is run by her students at University of Georgia, which is now the eighth year. There are hundreds of volunteers across [[North America]] in sampling wild monarchs for a debilitating disease.<ref name="tedxuga" />

Altizer held a number of administrative positions in the Odum School of Ecology, including Associate Dean for Academic Affairs (2012-2017), Academic Coordinator (2017-2019), Promotion and Tenure Chair (2020), and Associate Dean for Research and Operations (2020-2021). Most recently, she served as Interim Dean for the Odum School (2021-2023).{{Citation needed|date=December 2024}}

=== Research areas ===
Altizer's research interests are ecology of [[infectious diseases]] in natural populations, evolution of host resistance and [[parasite virulence]], insect ecology and [[evolution]], [[animal migration]]s, and [[Human impact on the environment|anthropogenic]] change and infectious disease dynamics.<ref name=ucdavis>{{cite web|url=http://entomology.ucdavis.edu/News/Sonia_Altizer__Migratory_Immunity__Parasite_Infection,_Host_Defense_and_Fitness_Costs_in_Monarch_Butterflies/|title=UC Davis Sonia Altizer|accessdate=March 2, 2015}}</ref>
